title: E2E: pinned EU org hitting US endpoint returns RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH + emits audit event
author: Leila Farouk
description:
Motivation: We’ve had a few beta pilots (and one Support escalation) where customers enabled EU pinning but were still calling the US base URL / had an SDK region mismatch. We need a stable end-to-end test that exercises the entire request admission path (gateway policy evaluation) and validates that we return the standardized error contract and also emit the required audit event evidence.

What this PR does: Adds E2E coverage for Hosted data residency enforcement when an org is pinned to EU (eu-west) but the request is sent to the US endpoint (us-east). The tests assert: (1) request is denied before model execution, (2) HTTP response includes machine-readable error code RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH and actionable remediation fields, and (3) an audit event residency.violation is emitted with the expected region + decision metadata.

Scope/Notes: Tests are designed to run against the CI E2E environment with the audit-test-sink enabled. We poll the audit sink with bounded retries to avoid flakes from async export. We also validate the response payload includes docs_url and suggested_region to match the SDK guidance.

Test cases included: - chat.completions: pinned EU org -> call us-east base URL -> expect 403 + RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH - embeddings: same as above - audit: verify residency.violation emitted within 30s with org_id, request_region, pinned_region, decision=deny, reason=region_mismatch

Out of scope: Cross-region override/exception behavior (covered by routing tests + exception process separately).

Rollout impact: None (tests only).

snippets:
Assertion highlights (chat):
- status_code == 403
- body.error.code == "RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH"
- body.error.details.pinned_region == "eu-west"
- body.error.details.request_region == "us-east"
- body.error.details.suggested_base_url contains "eu"

Audit verification:
- event.type == "residency.violation"
- event.actor.type == "api_key"
- event.resource.org_id == <test_org_id>
- event.residency.decision == "deny"
- event.residency.reason == "region_mismatch"

review_conversation:
Brian Murphy: Can we assert the exact error code + docs_url? We want to lock the contract for SDK exception typing.
Leila Farouk: Yep — added explicit assertions for error.code == RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH and that docs_url is present + points at /docs/security/data-residency#region-mismatch.

Amara Diallo: Please make sure the test is calling the US endpoint explicitly (not just setting a header) so we exercise gateway region selection.
Leila Farouk: Updated http client to use RW_E2E_US_BASE_URL for the mismatch call, and left EU base URL as control (not used here). Added a comment explaining this is to validate routing/admission behavior.

Kevin Osei: For audit events, can we validate minimum required fields for SIEM export (event_id, timestamp, org_id, region, decision)?
Leila Farouk: Added assertions for event_id + occurred_at presence and the residency.* fields. I kept it minimal to avoid coupling to exporter formatting beyond what we’ve documented in audit-events-data-residency.

Sean Gallagher: Concern about flakiness: polling for up to 30s is ok, but please use exponential backoff and surface useful debug output on timeout.
Leila Farouk: Implemented bounded exponential backoff (max 5s sleep) and dump the last 20 events seen from the sink on timeout to make failures actionable.

Benji Okafor: The org_factory change should ensure we don’t leak orgs/projects in shared test env. Are we cleaning up?
Leila Farouk: Added cleanup hooks to delete the project and org at the end of the test module; also added a unique suffix based on CI run id.
